source: Haas Automation, 'How to: Set a work offset with an edge finder and indicator', Haas Tip of the Day (YouTube -ZuRBppxRwU), 720p, downloaded through downr.org to C:\jigged-data\footage\ and analysed locally with MediaPipe Hand Landmarker; the video is not in the repo
method: trainual's motion/extract_hands.py, then its analyze_timing.py segmenting restricted to the windows where hands work the tools (the rest is talking to camera); the video is edited, so only uncut shots give durations

observed.what: The jog handle at .001: thumb under the rim, index and middle fingertips over it (GRASP precision disk). The handle has a spinner knob near its rim for fast moves and a dial graduated 0-100.
The right hand works the keys, then turns to the jog handle; the left hand stays off the pendant.
The test indicator hangs from an indicator holder in the spindle, not a magnetic base; the hand swings it round by turning the spindle nose.

used_for: vf2-controls: the jog handle's grasp, no longer proposed
dti-sweep-face: Haas's own mounting (in the spindle) recorded against the card's proposed magnetic-base seat
